core_obligations: The reduction to closed points: the author introduces the set X_0 of closed points of X and the sets U_{i,0} of closed points of the members of the covering, and records that X_0 intersected with U_i is contained in U_{i,0} while equality can fail in general (proof lines 3597-3601).

The forward direction: assuming each U_i is Jacobson, the proof shows X_0 intersected with U_i equals U_{i,0} by taking a point closed in U_i, looking at the closure of its singleton in X, and splitting into the cases whether the point lies in the other members of the covering (proof lines 3604-3612).

The identification of the two closed-point sets: the case analysis shows that the closure meets each U_j compatibly, which gives the claimed equality and hence that X is Jacobson (proof lines 3612-3630).

The converse and the union statement: if X is Jacobson then each U_i inherits the property, and in that case X_0 is the union of the U_{i,0}, which is the moreover clause of the statement (proof lines 3630-3639).
proof_roadmap: 先用闭点集 X_0 与各 U_i 的闭点集 U_{i,0} 建立 X_0 ∩ U_i ⊂ U_{i,0} 的包含（等式一般不成立）。
正向假设各 U_i 是 Jacobson，对 U_i 中闭点取其单点在 X 中的闭包，按该点落在哪些 U_j 中分类讨论，得到 X_0 ∩ U_i = U_{i,0}；反向由 X 的 Jacobson 性限制到各 U_i，并得到 X_0 = ∪ U_{i,0}。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the locality of the Jacobson property on an open covering (author lemma at source lines 3588-3594, label lemma-jacobson-local), including the identity X_0 = union of the U_{i,0}. The proof (source lines 3596-3639) is not the routine sheaf-theoretic locality argument: the author first records that the containment of closed-point sets can be strict for a single member of the covering (proof lines 3599-3601), and then recovers equality by a genuine case analysis on the closure of a point that is closed in one member of the covering and the way that closure meets the other members (proof lines 3604-3612). The converse direction is then formal, and the union statement is the by-product that the section uses. H2.
